transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-10-28 16:00 UTC — Duration 1:02:00
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Sofia Mendez (Redwood SE), Evan Park (CTO - Merchant Health), Maya Singh (Head of Infra), Priya Reddy (Security), Noah Kim (Platform Eng)

Summary: Quick scoping for a Private-network POC focusing on VPC peering vs PrivateLink, region lockdown, egress constraints and clear success criteria. Aim: define benchmarks, workload sizing, and timeline for a 4-week pilot.

Topics: POC success metrics, connectivity options (peering/privatelink), regional residency, egress lock, benchmark plan, timelines, artifacts requested.

Action items (recap): see action_items above.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Jordan, AE on the Redwood side, with Sofia our SE. how's everyone doing?
[00:18] Evan Park: Good thanks, uh, Evan here. we'll try to keep this tight, got a morning backlog.
[00:22] Maya Singh: Maya, hi. we're mainly focused on residency and no-egress constraints for PHI-adjacent telemetry.
[00:30] Jordan Lee: Totally, that's the main thing we wanted to confirm. Sofia, do you want to run through the high-level options — peering versus PrivateLink — and tradeoffs?
[00:40] Sofia Mendez: Yeah sure. So two primary topologies we commonly run: VPC peering which is simpler network-wise and gives L3 connectivity across accounts; PrivateLink (AWS PrivateLink / endpoint services) gives single-hop private endpoints and tighter egress control but can add latency and requires endpoint provisioning.
[01:02] Noah Kim: Can you quantify the latency delta? like ballpark ms?
[01:06] Sofia Mendez: In our internal numbers, peering tends to be sub-ms for co-region but across accounts depends on route tables; PrivateLink adds typically 5–15ms overhead in a lot of setups, sometimes more if cross-AZ. That's variable though, so we'll benchmark.
[01:25] Priya Reddy: The big policy requirement for us is that no PII or inference logs leave eu-west-1. We need egress locked down and KMS keys in our tenant.
[01:38] Jordan Lee: Understood. For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS and can pin region. We also do local audit logs — we can push logs to your S3 in-region, or forward to your logging endpoint via VPC.
[01:52] Evan Park: Are those audit logs realtime? we need them for compliance audits within 24 hours.
[01:58] Sofia Mendez: Yes, typically near real-time — there's buffering but retention and ingestion into your account is configurable. We'll include the exact flow in the security pack we send.
[02:10] Maya Singh: On connectivity, we're weighing maintenance overhead. Peering means route management and potential transitive routing concerns, PrivateLink is more explicit but we have to manage endpoint scaling.
[02:24] Jordan Lee: Also worth noting: peering gives you slightly better throughput for large batch workloads; PrivateLink can be easier to reason about for strict egress since traffic terminates at the endpoint service.
[02:38] Noah Kim: For our workload sizing — current estimates: 120 rps average, spikes to 400 rps, median payload size ~1.8KB, peak tokens per request ~1200. We're planning to run embeddings and chat completions.
[02:55] Sofia Mendez: Great. For that profile we'll simulate concurrent connections across a few nodes and measure tail latency. What are your latency SLOs?
[03:05] Evan Park: 95th percentile under 300ms for chat completions, ideally <200ms, and embeddings under 150ms 95th if possible.
[03:14] Sofia Mendez: That's reasonable but depends on model choice and topology. If you use a larger model we may need dedicated capacity for predictability. Also quantized variants can help cost/latency.
[03:28] Priya Reddy: On models — we're evaluating open-source families, not proprietary tokens, everything must run inside our VPC or region. No model weights allowed to leave.
[03:39] Jordan Lee: Redwood Private supports running model serving in your VPC / on-prem and you can keep weights behind your firewall. We will surface model variants for the POC that match your footprint.
[03:49] Maya Singh: Benchmarks — we want a baseline with our payload distribution, so realistic lengths, plus a synthetic worst-case. Can Redwood provide the harness to replay?
[03:58] Sofia Mendez: Yes we'll provide a benchmark harness and test scripts. We'll need sample payloads from you and expected concurrency timelines. We'll run against both peering and PrivateLink topologies and report throughput, 50/95/99 latencies, and token throughput per GPU.
[04:12] Evan Park: Also cost numbers — estimate per 1M tokens for the different topologies and quantization levels.
[04:19] Jordan Lee: We'll provide modeled unit economics for hosted vs Private. For the POC we can show the delta between peering (lower latency) and PrivateLink (easier egress control) including any endpoint costs.
[04:32] Noah Kim: One constraint — our corporate infra team refuses to open wide egress. We need explicit allow lists and no DNS leaks.
[04:40] Sofia Mendez: We can support IP allow lists, and for PrivateLink traffic doesn't egress to public internet. For peering, traffic flows over AWS backbone but you control route tables — no NAT necessary if configured correctly. We'll document the exact port ranges and CIDRs.
[04:56] Priya Reddy: Encryption at rest and in transit — KMS with customer keys, TLS mutual auth for internal endpoints?
[05:05] Sofia Mendez: We support customer-managed KMS (BYOK) and mTLS for operator APIs. We'll include certificate rotation in the runbook.
[05:12] Evan Park: Timeline — what's real for a POC? We want a pilot that runs benchmarks and validation in staging, then a production rollout. Goal: pilot in 4 weeks, evaluation week, then decision.
[05:24] Jordan Lee: That's feasible. Proposed plan: Week 0 — exchange artifacts (security pack, network details); Week 1 — deploy Private instance into your staging VPC (peering + PrivateLink configs); Week 2 — run bench harness; Week 3 — analyze results and tune; Week 4 — decision and SOW for dedicated.
[05:41] Maya Singh: Do you need credentials to our staging? we can provide a cross-account role and VPC peering request.
[05:47] Sofia Mendez: Cross-account role + peering accept is fine. For PrivateLink we'll need the endpoint service subscription and endpoint creation from your side. We'll provide Terraform snippets to make it repeatable.
[05:59] Noah Kim: Any compliance artifacts you can send now? like SOC2 cert, pen-test summary?
[06:05] Jordan Lee: Yes, we'll attach SOC2, ISO high-level, and our standard penetration test summary in the security pack. Also sample runbooks for incident response.
[06:16] Priya Reddy: Can you have a short checklist of items we need to sign off to consider the pilot successful?
[06:21] Sofia Mendez: We'll propose explicit success criteria: (1) 95th pct latency under 300ms for chat, under 150ms for embeddings for baseline traffic; (2) no traffic egress outside listed regions; (3) KMS customer keys used for all encryption; (4) audit logs delivered to Merchant Health account within 24 hours; (5) documented runbook for failover to fallback model.
[06:44] Evan Park: If those are met and cost is within modeled range, we'll greenlight a 6-month reserved capacity.
[06:51] Jordan Lee: Good. Any blockers we didn't cover?
[06:54] Maya Singh: One more — can you support region locking to a secondary DR region if we need it, and can that region be a different cloud region?
[07:03] Sofia Mendez: We support regional pinning per deployment; cross-cloud is more complex and will need additional network peering. We'll note that as an out-of-scope for the first pilot but can scope it in a follow up.
[07:15] Noah Kim: For benchmarking specifics — we'll test steady-state 120 rps for 1 hour, and a burst test to 400 rps for 10 minutes. Include tail-latency measurement at 99th percentile.
[07:27] Sofia Mendez: Perfect, we'll mirror that in our scripts. Also will run a cold start test for KV cache scenarios because your chat flow uses long contexts.
[07:36] Evan Park: Who will be our point of contact?
[07:38] Jordan Lee: I'll be primary for commercial and scheduling; Sofia will run technical. We'll loop in solutions engineering as needed.
[07:45] Priya Reddy: Please send the compliance questionnaire to me directly.
[07:48] Jordan Lee: Noted — sending to Priya.
[07:51] Evan Park: Sounds good. Last Q — competitive fit: are there features you provide that CloudVendorX doesn't?
[07:58] Sofia Mendez: Two differentiators: first, unified runtime across hosted and private so the same API and rollout tooling; second, smart routing and KV cache that reduce token costs at scale. We'll include comparative notes but not call names in the official pack.
[08:14] Jordan Lee: Ok let's recap next steps. We'll send security pack + SOW template, Sofia sends benchmark harness + terraform snippets. Merchant provides CIDRs, cross-account role, sample payloads and QPS numbers. Schedule pilot kickoff week of 2027-11-06.
[08:37] Evan Park: Agreed. Thanks everyone.
[08:40] Maya Singh: Thanks.
[08:41] Jordan Lee: Great talk soon, bye.

End of transcript.
